transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-03-12
- Start: 09:00 PT
- Duration: ~75 minutes (recording ended 10:15)
- Attendees: Lena, Diego, Priya, Omar, Connor, Maya, Ethan

Summary:
Quick technical retrospective on the RL optimizer regression that surfaced during the last dedicated cluster rollout. Go over timeline, hypothesis (quantization + kernel selection + new batching heuristic), immediate mitigations, and what to change in Q2 roadmap and launch readiness checklist. Action items assigned, and agreed next steps for a short postmortem and customer comms.

Topics & Notes:
09:00 Lena: Ok folks, thanks for joining, I know this is a lot today. We wanted to do a focused retro on the RL optimizer incident from last week and also fold that into our Q2 launch readiness checklist. I put a pretty tight agenda in the calendar: timeline, root cause hypotheses, mitigations, roadmap impact.

09:02 Diego: Quick update from infra, we had elevated tail latency starting 03-05 at 01:12 UTC on two dedicated pools after the quantized runtime was rolled. Autoscaler reacted but there was queueing and a few customer requests timed out. We rolled back at 03-05 03:40 UTC.

09:03 Omar: To add, our tracing showed long kernels during the attention path when sequence len hit ~2048. The new kernel selection logic favored an AVX-optimized path that looked cheaper but it introduced contention in our GPU dispatch queue. So it wasn't just quantization. There's an interaction with batching heuristics — K-V cache warmup also seemed to spike memory allocations.

09:05 Priya: Just to be clear. Are we confident this was a perf regression and not a model-quality issue? Support reported higher error rates but I suspect those are downstream timeouts, not model outputs.

09:06 Maya: Right, the evals we've run so far don't show quality drift. The token-level scoring stays consistent. The "higher error" was from the clients retrying and getting 504/timeout, so we saw duplicate requests and queue amplification.

09:08 Connor: I tried reproducing locally but our bench machines don't match the dedicated pool scheduling. Two notes: 1) our quantized build picks a different matmul kernel when batch size is 1 and seq len > 1024; 2) the continuous batching code merged some prefixes which increased overall peak memory footprint. Both are plausible levers.

09:10 Ethan: There's also an operational angle: our canary thresholds were purely p99 latency, and didn't include kernel-level errors or queue-depth telemetry. That slowed detection.

09:12 Diego: Timeline reconstructed: deploy -> spike -> alert at 01:18 -> attempt scale up -> partial mitigation -> rollback at 03:40. During the spike we had two fallback routes enabled but the traffic routing policy kept preferring the newer variant because capacity signals were noisy.

09:14 Lena: Okay, hypothesis list: A) kernel selection change + quantization interaction causes dispatch lockups under long sequences; B) batching heuristic increases memory pressure and leads to slower kernel execution; C) autoscaler/route policy misconfiguration prolonged exposure. Which of these do folks buy?

09:15 Omar: I buy A and B. C is a process/config issue — true but lower priority for immediate fix.

09:16 Maya: Agree — A seems primary. We should validate with profile traces. Connor, can you get the traces we need?

09:17 Connor: Yep. I need reproducer inputs; Maya can provide a short eval set with varied sequence lengths. I will run the quantized binary + old binary and capture NVTX and kernel timelines. Expect first pass by 03-16.

09:19 (small crosstalk) Diego: Also, Omar, can you confirm whether the K-V cache warmup strategy was changed in the release? I thought the default was 2-step warmup but we moved to eager warmup for throughput gains.

09:20 Omar: We did change warmup; we enabled eager warmup on dedicated clusters to reduce first-token latency, but that increases memory churn. I'll dump the config and diff it.

09:22 Priya: From a product perspective, what's the impact to our Q2 release milestones if we need to hold this and add more verification? We have partner integrations scheduled in mid April.

09:23 Lena: We don't want a blanket hold. We want to add a gating checklist for long-sequence workloads: kernel-level smoke, KV cache smoke, and a targeted perf run. If those pass we can proceed. If not, we throttle rollout and notify partner stakeholders.

09:25 Maya: For gating, propose: 1) deterministic perf benchmark for seq lengths [512,1024,2048], 2) KV cache stress test with cold/warm scenarios, 3) memory pressure test with quantized builds. I can own the eval harness.

09:27 Connor: Also add a short test to detect kernel path divergence: run matrix of batch size * seq len and compare chosen kernels against baseline. If kernel selection deviates, flag.

09:29 Diego: Operational changes: add a queue-depth alarm and kernel-error counter to canary dashboards. We should reduce canary traffic ramp to 10% until these checks are green.

09:31 Lena: Good. On customer comms: we need a short public-facing summary explaining what happened, impact, mitigation, and next steps. Not a full postmortem yet, that comes later. Support team will need the summary + FAQs. Ethan, can you coordinate?

09:32 Ethan: Yep. I'll draft and run it by Lena and legal if needed. Target to publish to CSM & support slack channel by 03-14.

09:34 (pause, keyboard clacking)

09:36 Diego: Quick question on rollout policy: the routing fallback behaved oddly — the control plane kept preferring new variant even with rising latency because we weigh cost over latency for some tiers. We need to adjust conservative routing for enterprise customers.

09:38 Priya: We should surface two configurable flags per customer: prefer_cost vs prefer_latency and an emergency override. For now, lock enterprise to prefer_latency for 48 hours post-canary.

09:40 Maya: Regarding regression alerts, we also should tie quality monitoring: if retries spike > X% for a customer for Y minutes, auto-fail canary. Right now retries are invisible in the canary guard.

09:42 Connor: From a dev side, short-term fixes: 1) revert eager K-V warmup on dedicated, 2) revert kernel selector tweak or add a guard for seq_len>1024, 3) increase memory budget on the quantized path to avoid OOM thrash. We'll test each independently.

09:45 Omar: On the SRE side, we'll prepare a canary plan: reduced ramp, added telemetry, and a rollback playbook. We'll also run a chaos-style test that injects a delayed dispatch to see how autoscaler behaves.

09:47 Lena: Anything else that should go into the postmortem? Costs, impact to SLAs, customers affected, timeline, root cause and corrective actions. Also link to traces + diffs.

09:48 Diego: I'll also add the autoscaler decision logs so we can see why it didn't prefer fallback faster.

09:50 (brief side conversation about test infra availability)

09:53 Maya: One risk callout: if we widen memory budgets for quantized path, we may increase overall cost per token. We need tradeoff analysis: immediate stability vs unit economics. This belongs in the Q2 plan as a temporary mitigation.

09:55 Priya: For roadmap changes: we propose shifting the long-sequence-optimizations epic earlier in Q2, and adding a "Launch gating & telemetry" spike to sprint-18. That will push a few non-critical perf items to later in Q2.

09:57 Lena: Ok, decision: do gating + short-term revert on warmup + telemetry, then resume canary with low ramp. If gating passes we continue rollout. If not, rollback and run deeper perf work.

09:59 Connor: I will attempt reproducer by 03-16 and post traces. If I hit a blocker will ping #infra-runs.

10:01 Omar: I'll prepare the rollback playbook and run a smoke test for KV cache scenarios on staging by 03-15.

10:03 Ethan: I'll draft the customer summary and include a short FAQ for CSMs; target 03-14 for internal preview.

10:05 Lena: Anything from legal or compliance to be aware of? We had no data exposure, this is performance only. We'll still check with security for logs sharing.

10:07 Maya: One more technical note: the quantized path changed how we pack tensors; that could change memory alignment and cause noise. I'll add that to the list.

10:09 Diego: Planning note — we'll add a new checklist item to require kernel-level smoke in our release playbook starting immediately.

10:11 (wrap-up)

10:12 Lena: Recap: Action items assigned (see agenda). Postmortem draft by 03-14, reproduce/perf traces by 03-16, targeted fixes and canary plan by 03-17/18. We'll reconvene next Wednesday 03-19 for a checkpoint. Thanks everyone.

10:13 Connor: Thanks.

10:14 Omar: Thanks, bye.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcript picked up some terms wrong ("KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash", "kernel" as "colonel" a few times). Names occasionally labeled as Speaker 3. We kept original speaker labels where clear.
